instructions.content: Describe the diagram specifically: ALWAYS include the type, components, flow or direction, labels and style, with element names, relationships and notation conventions; avoid vague prompts such as 'Make a flowchart'.
ALWAYS pass the --doc-type flag matching the target venue (journal 8.5, conference 8.0, poster 7.0, presentation 6.5) so the correct quality threshold applies.
NEVER set --iterations higher than 2; smart iteration stops early once the threshold is met.
Set ANTHROPIC_API_KEY in the environment before running the generation script.
NEVER hardcode the API key in source or task files.
Store generated diagrams in the figures/ subfolder.
Rely on smart iteration: review each image against the document-type threshold, stop when the score meets it, and regenerate with an improved prompt only if it falls below.
Use the threshold table: journal 8.5, conference 8.0, thesis 8.0, grant 8.0, preprint 7.5, report 7.5, poster 7.0, presentation 6.5, default 7.5.
NEVER use this skill for data plots such as bar charts, scatter plots or heatmaps; use a plotting library.
Do not use this skill when a figure must be reproduced exactly from a prior publication; use the original source or a vector redraw tool.
Do not use this skill for interactive or animated diagrams; it produces static publication images only.
NEVER skip the --doc-type flag for formal submissions, because the default 7.5 threshold is lower than the journal 8.5 threshold.
Use colourblind-friendly colours (Okabe-Ito palette), a clean light background, high contrast and sans-serif labels.
Prefer vector output (PDF for LaTeX, SVG for web) or 300+ DPI raster, with line weights of at least 0.5 pt.
Caption every diagram thoroughly, include it with \includegraphics, and reference it in the text.
Keep the prompts and generated images in version control.
Verify the result against the threshold using the review log (score, critique, early-stop reason) before reporting completion.
Confirm the API key is set before any generation by checking the environment variable.
Use verbose mode (-v) when the generation and review steps should be shown.
